title: Programmable Systems & Programming Languages
description: Microcontrollers, PLCs, and the three types of programming language used in programmable electronic systems.
content_html:
What Makes a System Programmable?

A programmable system differs from a fixed (hard-wired) circuit because its behaviour is controlled by software — a set of instructions stored in memory — rather than by the physical arrangement of components alone. In a hard-wired circuit, changing what the circuit does means physically re-wiring it. In a programmable system, the same hardware can be given an entirely new function by rewriting the program. This flexibility is one of the greatest advantages of programmable systems in engineering design.

Microcontrollers

A microcontroller is a compact integrated circuit containing a processor (CPU), program memory (flash), data memory (RAM), and configurable input/output (I/O) pins — all on a single chip. It reads inputs from sensors and switches, executes a stored program, and produces outputs to control actuators and displays. Well-known microcontroller platforms include the Arduino (using the ATmega328P) and the BBC micro:bit. Microcontrollers are ideal for low-power, low-cost, embedded applications where a full computer would be excessive — for example, a smart thermostat, a traffic light controller, or an automatic plant watering system.

The advantages of using a microcontroller include: flexibility (the program can be changed without hardware alteration); reduced component count (one chip replaces many logic ICs); low cost for mass production; and reliability (no moving parts). The disadvantages include: the need for programming skills to write or modify the code; dependence on a power supply that does not fail; and potential vulnerability to software bugs that can cause unpredictable behaviour.

Key Fact

Advantages of a programmable system over hard-wired: easily reprogrammed, reduced component count, flexible for multiple applications, easier to update or correct. Disadvantages: requires programming knowledge, relies on power supply stability, software bugs can cause faults, initial setup is more complex than simple hard-wired circuits.

Programmable Logic Controllers (PLCs)

A Programmable Logic Controller (PLC) is a specialised industrial microcontroller built for harsh environments — it is designed to be shock-resistant, tolerant of temperature extremes and electromagnetic interference, and capable of controlling multiple high-power outputs simultaneously. PLCs are programmed using ladder logic (a graphical language resembling relay circuit diagrams) or structured text, and are used extensively in factories, water treatment plants, and automated assembly lines. Compared to a general-purpose microcontroller, a PLC is more expensive, but far more robust and better suited to safety-critical industrial environments where reliability is paramount.

Types of Programming Language and Systems

OCR R047 specifies three types of programming language or system. A text-based language (such as Python, C, or C++) uses written code consisting of commands, variables, and syntax rules. It is the most powerful and flexible option, offering full control over system behaviour, but requires the programmer to learn the language syntax and is harder for beginners to read. A block-based editor (such as Scratch, MakeCode, or MIT App Inventor) represents program instructions as visual blocks that snap together, eliminating syntax errors and making logic easy to see — ideal for beginners and for teaching purposes, but less efficient for complex programs. A flowchart system (such as Flowol or similar graphical tools) uses standard flowchart symbols (start/stop ovals, process rectangles, decision diamonds) connected by arrows to represent program logic — visual and easy to plan, but can become cluttered for large programs and is not used in professional development.

Key Fact

Text-based: most flexible, full control, but requires syntax knowledge and harder for beginners. Block-based: no syntax errors, visually clear, easy for beginners, but less efficient for complex tasks. Flowchart: easy to plan logic visually, but cluttered for large programs and not used professionally. The OCR specification does not require you to write code in any specific language.

A microcontroller (e.g. Arduino, micro:bit) is a low-cost, compact chip typically used in prototyping, educational projects, and consumer electronics. It is programmed via a USB connection from a laptop and runs on 3.3 V or 5 V. A PLC is a larger, more expensive, industrial-grade unit designed for continuous operation in electrically noisy factory environments — it operates from 24 V DC or 110/240 V AC, has screw-terminal I/O connections for industrial wiring, and is built to safety standards that a microcontroller does not meet. For a school project controlling LEDs and a buzzer, a microcontroller is entirely suitable. For controlling a bottling plant's conveyor and filling machines that must run 24 hours a day without failure, a PLC is the appropriate choice.

When an OCR exam question asks you to recommend a programming language type, consider the user's experience and the complexity of the task. A Year 7 student creating a simple flashing LED sequence: block-based editor — no syntax to learn, immediate visual feedback, drag-and-drop makes it accessible. A university engineer writing firmware for a commercial product: text-based language (C or Python) — full control over memory and timing, code can be optimised, and it integrates with professional toolchains. A teacher planning the logic of a new control system before implementation: flowchart system — easy to map out decision trees and loops before writing any code, acts as a design document. The OCR specification requires you to compare the relative merits for a given application — always state why the chosen type suits the context, not just what its general advantages are.
exam_tip_html: When evaluating microcontrollers versus hard-wired circuits, the most creditworthy points are specific: say 'the microcontroller can be reprogrammed without changing the hardware, so if the client changes the specification the engineer only needs to upload new code' rather than 'it is more flexible'. For programming language questions, always relate your answer to the specific application in the question — a beginner student and a professional engineer need different tools, and you must explain why. The OCR specification explicitly excludes writing actual programs, so you will never be asked to produce code.
conclusion_html:
Key Takeaways

  • A programmable system stores its behaviour as software, allowing the same hardware to be reprogrammed for different tasks — unlike a hard-wired circuit which must be physically altered to change its function.
  • Microcontrollers (compact, low-cost, flexible) suit prototyping and consumer electronics; PLCs (rugged, industrial-grade, expensive) suit continuous factory and safety-critical environments.
  • Three programming types: text-based (powerful, requires syntax knowledge), block-based (visual, beginner-friendly, no syntax errors), and flowchart (good for planning logic, not used professionally) — choose based on the user's experience and the complexity of the task.

glossary_terms.definition: An electronic system whose behaviour is determined by a stored program that can be changed without altering the hardware.
A single integrated circuit that contains a processor, memory, and programmable input/output peripherals, used to control electronic systems.
A ruggedised industrial computer designed to control manufacturing processes, machinery, and production lines in real-time, programmed using ladder logic or similar languages.
A visual programming environment in which instructions are represented as graphical blocks that snap together, eliminating syntax errors and making logic easy to follow.

practice_questions.text:
Which of the following best describes a programmable system?
A) A circuit with components wired in a fixed arrangement that cannot be changed.
B) A system whose behaviour is defined by a stored program that can be rewritten.
C) A system that uses only analogue signals and no digital components.
D) A system controlled entirely by mechanical switches.
practice_questions.marks: B) A system whose behaviour is defined by a stored program that can be rewritten. [1 mark]

practice_questions.text: State two advantages of using a microcontroller instead of a hard-wired circuit to control a security alarm system.
practice_questions.marks: One mark each for any two from: the microcontroller can be reprogrammed without changing the hardware if requirements change; it replaces many separate logic ICs with a single chip, reducing component count and cost; the behaviour can be updated remotely or via a USB connection; it can process multiple inputs and control multiple outputs simultaneously. [2 marks]

practice_questions.text: Explain one difference between a microcontroller and a Programmable Logic Controller (PLC), giving a suitable application for each.
practice_questions.marks: 1 mark: a microcontroller is compact, low-cost, and runs at low voltage — a PLC is ruggedised, more expensive, and designed for harsh industrial environments. 1 mark: suitable microcontroller application — e.g. a smart thermostat, an Arduino-based LED display, or a school prototyping project. 1 mark: suitable PLC application — e.g. controlling a factory conveyor system, a water treatment plant pump, or an automated bottling line. [3 marks]

practice_questions.text: Describe the three types of programming language or system used with programmable components. For each type, give one advantage and one disadvantage.
practice_questions.marks: Award up to 4 marks. Text-based language: advantage — most powerful and flexible, full control over system behaviour / disadvantage — requires knowledge of syntax, harder for beginners (1 mark for advantage + disadvantage correctly paired to text-based). Block-based editor: advantage — no syntax errors, visual and accessible for beginners / disadvantage — less efficient for complex programs (1 mark for correctly paired). Flowchart system: advantage — easy to plan logic visually using standard symbols / disadvantage — becomes cluttered for large programs, not used in professional development (1 mark for correctly paired). 1 additional mark for clear, developed descriptions that go beyond single-word answers. Maximum 4 marks. [4 marks total]

practice_questions.text:
A design engineering company is creating a new automated greenhouse system that monitors temperature and light levels, controls heating, ventilation fans, and grow lights, and can be reprogrammed by the user if crop requirements change.

Discuss the suitability of using a microcontroller as the programmable component in this system.
practice_questions.marks:
Mastering (5–6 marks): a balanced discussion that covers at least two factors with development. For: a microcontroller is well-suited because it can read analogue sensor inputs (NTC thermistor for temperature, LDR for light) via its ADC, and control multiple outputs (heater relay, fan motor, grow light LED) via its I/O pins simultaneously — all from a single compact, low-cost chip that can be reprogrammed in-field if crop requirements change (developed, applied to scenario). Against/limitation: a microcontroller is not inherently rugged — in a greenhouse environment with high humidity and temperature extremes, the microcontroller may need to be housed in a sealed enclosure to prevent moisture damage; if reliability is critical and the system must run 24/7 without downtime, a PLC might be more appropriate despite higher cost (limitation developed, counter-argument applied). A recommendation with justification: a microcontroller with appropriate protective housing is suitable for this application given its flexibility, low cost, and ability to be reprogrammed by the user.
Secure (3–4 marks): two factors identified and briefly explained with some reference to the scenario.
Developing (2 marks): one factor identified with limited explanation.
Emerging (1 mark): a single relevant point with no development. [6 marks]

practice_questions.text:
An engineering tutor is planning a unit of work in which students of varying experience will all program a microcontroller to control a set of traffic lights. The class includes complete beginners, students with some experience of block-based tools, and one advanced student who has used Python before.

Evaluate the suitability of text-based, block-based, and flowchart programming approaches for this class, and recommend which approach the tutor should use.
practice_questions.marks:
Mastering (7–8 marks): a balanced evaluation that covers all three approaches with specific application to the mixed-experience class scenario and a clear recommendation with justification. Text-based (e.g. Python/C++): most powerful and used professionally — the advanced student would benefit and learn transferable skills, but complete beginners will struggle with syntax errors and debugging, potentially causing disengagement; not suitable as the primary approach for a mixed-ability class (developed, applied). Block-based (e.g. MakeCode/Scratch): no syntax errors, visual representation maps well to traffic light sequencing logic, all ability levels can access it, and the advanced student can still challenge themselves by exploring loops and conditionals within the block environment — most suitable for the majority of the class (developed, justified for the scenario). Flowchart: useful for planning the traffic light sequence before programming, and all students can engage with it regardless of prior experience — but it is not a programming language per se and cannot directly control a microcontroller, so it should be used as a design planning tool rather than the implementation method (limitation clearly identified). Recommendation: use block-based as the primary programming environment for all students; use flowchart as a design/planning step before implementation; allow the advanced student to optionally translate their block program into Python for extension work. This recommendation should be clearly justified with reference to the mixed-ability context.
Secure (5–6 marks): all three types evaluated with application and a clear recommendation.
Developing (3–4 marks): two types covered with some application, limited recommendation.
Emerging (1–2 marks): basic points, no recommendation. [8 marks]

knowledge_checks.q: Which of the following is the main advantage of a programmable system over a hard-wired circuit?
options: Its behaviour can be changed by rewriting the stored program without altering hardware
It always produces analogue output signals

knowledge_checks.q: Which type of programmable component is most suitable for controlling machinery on a factory production line?
A block-based programming editor eliminates _____ errors, making it accessible to beginners.
A microcontroller contains a processor, program memory, data memory, and configurable _____ pins.
Match each programming type to its key characteristic.
right: Uses standard symbols such as ovals, rectangles, and diamonds to represent logic
Written code using commands and syntax — most powerful and flexible
Visual blocks that snap together — no syntax errors, beginner-friendly

flashcard_questions.q: What is the key difference between a programmable system and a hard-wired circuit?
flashcard_questions.a: A programmable system stores its behaviour as software that can be changed without altering the hardware.

flashcard_questions.q: What four main elements are integrated onto a single microcontroller chip?
flashcard_questions.a: A microcontroller contains a processor (CPU), program memory (flash), data memory (RAM), and I/O pins.

flashcard_questions.q: Give two advantages of using a microcontroller compared to separate logic ICs.
flashcard_questions.a: A microcontroller reduces component count, lowers cost, and can be reprogrammed without hardware changes.

flashcard_questions.q: What is a Programmable Logic Controller (PLC) and where is it typically used?
flashcard_questions.a: A PLC is a ruggedised industrial computer used to control factory machinery, conveyors, and automated processes.

flashcard_questions.q: Give one advantage of a PLC over a microcontroller in an industrial setting.
flashcard_questions.a: A PLC is designed to withstand harsh environments — heat, vibration, and electrical noise — where a microcontroller may fail.

flashcard_questions.q: What is one advantage of a text-based programming language over a block-based editor?
flashcard_questions.a: A text-based language offers full control and flexibility, and can handle complex programs more efficiently.

flashcard_questions.q: What is one disadvantage of a text-based programming language for a beginner?
flashcard_questions.a: A text-based language requires knowledge of syntax rules, and syntax errors will prevent the program from running.

flashcard_questions.q: What is one advantage of a block-based editor compared to a text-based language?
flashcard_questions.a: A block-based editor eliminates syntax errors because valid blocks snap together, making it accessible for beginners.

flashcard_questions.q: What standard symbols are used in a flowchart programming system?
flashcard_questions.a: Flowcharts use ovals for start/stop, rectangles for processes, and diamonds for decision points, connected by arrows.

flashcard_questions.q: Give one disadvantage of using a flowchart system for large programs.
flashcard_questions.a: Flowcharts become cluttered and difficult to follow for large programs, and are not used in professional development.

flashcard_questions.q: Give one example of a microcontroller platform used in educational and prototyping contexts.
flashcard_questions.a: The Arduino and the BBC micro:bit are both widely used microcontroller platforms for education and prototyping.

flashcard_questions.q: What does the OCR specification explicitly exclude from the requirements for programming languages?
flashcard_questions.a: OCR explicitly excludes writing or producing actual programs in any specific language or system.
